captions.text: Almost every quant fund forces its portfolio to be industry-neutral.
One of the world's largest asset managers even told regulators why:
sector bets don't add value.
But claims like that are almost never tested in the open.
The data is expensive, and most backtests quietly leak the future.
So we rebuilt the model from free public filings.
2.7 million facts, each used only after it became public,
with the test period locked in code before we looked.
And you can explore all of it.
Switch the universe, the peer definition, or the time period,
and every statistic is recomputed live.
In the locked test, industry bets earned a Sharpe ratio of 0.68.
The claim survives, but only narrowly.
Then the twist.
The market-neutral book wasn't neutral.
Its real market beta was 0.15.
Hedge it out, and the Sharpe falls to 0.46.
In 3D, watch industries move month by month,
and see which stocks really trade together.
Nearly half of the statistical peer groups cross official sectors.
Who is your peer?
Open research, pre-registered, with every bug on the record.
Link in the comments.
